newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev firms to 2,700-2,800 vs dlr at close.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev firms to 2,700-2,800 vs dlr at close.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev firmed gently to 2,700-2,800 per dollar at the close from the morning's 2,800-2,950 due to a fall in foreign currency demand, dealers said.
"Trade turned very light after final clients, who bid for dollars in the morning, left the market in the early afternoon," one dealer said.

An attempt to break through the 3,000 level failed today due to the fall in demand, but the lev could easily slide to 3,100 again in the next few days amid the ongoing low dollar liquidity of the interbank market, another dealer said.
High dollar demand pressured the lev to an all-time low of 3,100 at midday on Tuesday.

The retail market lev/dollar exchange rate, which lagged behind the interbank market in the past several days due to low lev liquidity, today caught up as a result of increased dollar buying, dealers said.
The dollar was bid around 2200 levs and was offered near 2800 in late afternoon against bids of 1800 and asks of 2200 late on Wednesday.
"Clients were withdrawing levs from banks to buy foreign currency from exchange shops where the dollar was offered at 2,500-2,700 by midday," an exchange bureau trader said.
Commercial banks were also buying cheaper dollars from exchange shops, he added. -- Anastas Petrov, Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
